node.title: Denominator-root cancellation and puncture-trivialization dichotomy
node.closure: exact same-owner source decomposition after common-pole cancellation
node.statement: After exact common-pole cancellation in a source-normalized rational atom, the nonzero-scalar indices split canonically into reduced support-wise MCA witnesses and puncture-trivialized indices. The former retain the same received-line and slope owner in the reduced root-free certificate. For every trivialized index, because t<=m-k, polynomial uniqueness forces h_i=p0_i+gamma_i p1_i globally; on the deleted pole set P the defect vectors u_i=r0-p0_i and v_i=r1-p1_i obey u_i+gamma_i v_i=0 with v_i nonzero, so the slope is recovered from the defect. Distinct slopes cannot share the same ordered polynomial pair (p0_i,p1_i). The split is exhaustive and disjoint but gives no bound on the number of defect records and does not prove exception routing.
